function: Downlink beamforming for cell-free mMIMO (CJT, PCJT, NCJT) via GCN-based deep unfolding of R-WMMSE, trained to maximize weighted sum rate (pp. 1, 9, 11).
system: Cell-free mMIMO downlink, TDD; 9 APs with 64 antennas, 3 UEs with 2 antennas, two streams per UE, 1x1 km; no RIS; band not stated (pp. 4, 12).
method: Deep unfolding of R-WMMSE into 7 layers: graph convolutional filter for W-block, complex GCN layer for F-block, skip connections; unsupervised SGD on negative WSR loss (pp. 9-13).
data_channel: Custom simulation: Weichselberger Rician correlated channels, COST 321 Walfish-Ikegami path loss; 5000 random AP/UE layouts for training, 1000 for validation; no public dataset (pp. 5, 11-12).
test_conditions: Trained and validated on random layouts from the same area; WSR swept over iterations, pilot reuse, K=4-12 UEs, layers; training versus test K not stated (pp. 12-14).
baselines: Non-learned WMMSE [29] and R-WMMSE [13] in each transmission mode; learned only the authors' own G-WMMSE (GCN unfolding of WMMSE); no earlier learned method (pp. 12-14).
metrics: Weighted sum rate, training loss, CPU time per iteration, test time, training time per step, AP-CPU interaction size (pp. 12-14).
complexity: Trainable parameters L(4F+G+1)+(L-1)F^2 (p. 11); WMMSE per-iteration O(|Mk|Nt^3) (p. 8); test time 0.81 s versus 3.95 s for WMMSE (Table VI, p. 14).
q1_support: p. 5: "we adopt the Weichselberger Rician channel"; p. 11: "follows the COST 321 Walfish-Ikegami" applies to the large-scale path loss only. Custom simulator; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 12: "We generate 5000 random realizations of AP and UE" layouts for training and 1000 for validation, same distribution. p. 14: "In Fig. 9, the achieved WSR performance is given with" varying K, but no training at another K or retraining is stated.
q3_support: p. 12: "Fig. 3 illustrates the WSR performance for WMMSE and" R-WMMSE (non-learned). p. 14: "proposed and validated GCN-based unfolding architectures" for WMMSE and R-WMMSE, so G-WMMSE is the authors' own variant; no earlier learned beamformer is compared.
q4_support: p. 11: "the G&R-WMMSE architecture comprises" L(4F + G + 1) + (L - 1)F^2 trainable parameters; p. 14: "In Table VI, we compare the average CPU" time of the algorithms (test time 0.81 s for G&R-WMMSE).
q5_support: p. 12: "We generate 5000 random realizations of AP and UE" layouts for training, so the data are simulated. No code or data link appears, and no public dataset or measured data is used.
notes: COST 321 Walfish-Ikegami gives only the large-scale path loss (p. 11) and the small-scale channel is a custom Weichselberger Rician model, so q1 is 0; the reviewer may confirm. G-WMMSE is presented as the authors' own GCN unfolding of WMMSE (p. 14) and is attributed to no earlier paper, so it is a variant of the proposed method and q3 is 0; if the reviewer finds it is the architecture of reference [33], q3 would change. Deep unfolding with trained parameters counts as learned. The text gives L = 16 AP antennas for Fig. 3 while Table IV (p. 12) gives 64.
